extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent practitioners, and applicants (handling secrecy, access, national security, and foreign filing)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal/regulatory standards governing confidentiality, public access, national-security-related handling, foreign filing licenses, and statements to DOE/NASA for U.S. patent applications, including procedures for telephone/in-person requests and file handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of pending patent applications (35 U.S.C. 122(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in subsection (b), applications for patents shall be kept in confidence by the Patent and Trademark Office and no information concerning the same given without authority of the applicant or owner unless necessary to carry out provisions of an Act of Congress or in special circumstances determined by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent applications that have not been published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) are generally preserved in confidence pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(a). Information concerning filing, pendency, subject matter, and access will only be given as set forth in §1.11 or §1.14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of applications (35 U.S.C. 122(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to exceptions, each application shall be published promptly after expiration of 18 months from the earliest filing date for which benefit is sought; an applicant may request earlier publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director establishes procedures. The Director's determination to release or not release information concerning a published application is final and nonreviewable. An applicant can request nonpublication at filing and may rescind such request; filing certain foreign applications without timely notice can cause abandonment unless delay shown unintentional. Redacted copies may be submitted when corresponding foreign filings are less extensive; section 154(d) does not apply to claims lacking enabling description in the redacted publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to publication
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall not be published if it is (i) no longer pending; (ii) subject to a secrecy order under section 181; (iii) a provisional application filed under 111(b); or (iv) an application for a design patent filed under chapter 16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonpublication requests per statute and procedures must be followed; rescission and foreign filing notice rules apply (45-day notice requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication protest and pre-issuance opposition protection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall establish procedures to ensure no protest or other form of pre-issuance opposition to the grant of a patent may be initiated after publication without the express written consent of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants control initiation of post-publication protests absent their written consent; internal USPTO procedures implement this statutory protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: National security nonpublication and secrecy orders
rubrics_metrics.description: No application shall be published if the publication or disclosure would be detrimental to national security; Director shall establish procedures to promptly identify such applications and maintain secrecy in accordance with chapter 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy Orders under 35 U.S.C. 181 are used to prevent publication and to require special handling; identification and referral procedures to appropriate agencies (and chapter 17 rules) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access categories for public availability (37 CFR 1.14(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Records associated with patent applications may be available to the public in specific situations: (i) patented applications and statutory invention registrations; (ii) published abandoned applications; (iii) published pending applications; (iv) unpublished abandoned applications that are identified or relied upon; (v) unpublished pending applications whose benefit is claimed; (vi) unpublished pending applications that are incorporated by reference or otherwise identified; (vii) cases where a petition for access or a power to inspect is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each category has distinct procedural and fee requirements (e.g., copies upon request and payment under §1.19(b)); redacted copies may limit content for published pending applications if a redacted publication was used. The Office will not provide access to the paper file of a pending application except as provided in paragraphs (c) or (h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Status information that may be communicated to the public (37 CFR 1.14(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The information that may be communicated (i.e., status information) includes: (i) whether the application is pending, abandoned, or patented; (ii) whether the application has been published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b); (iii) the application numerical identifier; and (iv) whether another application claims the benefit of the application and status information for such applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerical identifier may be the eight-digit application number or the six-digit serial number plus certain date fields. Only the listed items constitute status information; other continuity data (e.g., CIP, continuation/divisional status, abandonment dates) may be confidential and must not be communicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/limits of 'status information'
rubrics_metrics.description: Status information means only: (A) whether the application is pending, abandoned, or patented; (B) whether it has been published; (C) the application number or serial number plus a filing/entry date; (D) whether another application claims the benefit of the application (with specified status information for those applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters should be directed to PAIR or FIU for status inquiries. PALM Intranet is used internally to verify and determine status. The rule applies only to subsequent and not prior applications in a chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who is entitled to status information for unpublished applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester is entitled to status information if the requester is (A) an inventor; (B) an attorney or agent of record; (C) an assignee of record; or (D) a person with written authority from (A),(B), or (C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not one of these categories, status information may be provided only if the application is identified in a published patent document or other specified identification conditions are met; require written request and supporting published document (with translation if not English).

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone and in-person verification procedure before disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Before any information about an unpublished pending or abandoned application is given over the telephone or in person, the identity of the requester must be adequately verified following specified steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: (A) obtain caller's full name, application number, and telephone number; ask if there is an attorney/agent of record and request registration number; (B) verify release authorization via PALM Intranet or application file; (C) return the call using verified telephone numbers (release only to attorney/agent phone from PALM, or to applicant's verified phone if no agent). For in-person, ask requester to wait while verifying identification. If association cannot be verified, do not release information and inform the caller that verification failed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PALM/PAIR/FIU to verify and provide status information
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters should check PAIR on the USPTO website; FIU will check Office records and inform the requester of publication/issue status. PALM Intranet should be used to verify registration numbers, correspondence addresses, and application assignment to Technology Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PALM Intranet is the internal authoritative source for contact and status verification. FIU will request published patent documents when necessary and will accept facsimile or written correspondence including return address/fax number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on revealing continuity/chain details
rubrics_metrics.description: Other information contained on internal screens (e.g., whether application is a CIP, continuation or divisional, date of abandonment, issue date) may be confidential information and should not be communicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the status information items listed in 37 CFR 1.14(a)(2) should be given to unauthorized requesters; internal continuity data must be withheld unless requester is authorized or proper identification/requests presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of status information when requester supplies published patent document
rubrics_metrics.description: If a non-authorized requester provides a written request including a copy of a published patent document which refers to the specific application (or translation), the requester is entitled to status information for the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published patent document must identify the application by application number or serial number and filing date; if not in English, a translation of the pertinent part must be included. The published document may be presented in person, by facsimile, or in written correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to unpublished applications identified in the file of another application
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is identified in the file contents of another application but not the published patent application or patent itself, a granted petition for access or a power to inspect is necessary to obtain the application or a copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions for access follow the procedures in paragraph (h) (petition for access) or a power to inspect under paragraph (c); requester must follow petition process and, if granted, appropriate fees apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone release rules when attorney/agent of record exists
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is an attorney or agent of record, information should only be released by calling the attorney’s or agent’s telephone number obtained from PALM Intranet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept caller-supplied attorney phone numbers without verification via PALM. If registration number is provided, use PALM to verify and retrieve contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of papers and physical security obligations for USPTO employees
rubrics_metrics.description: All USPTO employees are legally obligated to preserve pending applications in confidence until published or patented; employees must exercise care transporting applications, use appropriate envelopes for interoffice mail, not reproduce application parts except for official purposes, and not remove files from USPTO premises except with Director authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authorization to remove files is given, the employee having custody is responsible for maintaining confidentiality. Files must not be placed in desk drawers or overlooked; whenever an application (or IFW artifact) is removed from an operating area a charge on the PALM system must be promptly made. Official papers accepted only at a central delivery window except specified exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on reproducing or copying application parts
rubrics_metrics.description: No part of any application or paper related thereto should be reproduced or copied except for official purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unauthorized copying or distribution may implicate criminal statutes (18 U.S.C. 2071) and internal disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone/in-person handling when publication/issue dates appear to be in the future
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular care should be exercised when a request is made for the publication date or publication number, or issue date and patent number assigned to a pending patent application; if the publication or issue date is later than the current date, such information may be given only to the applicant, assignee of record, or attorney/agent of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify identity before disclosing future publication/issue dates; caller must be verified per standard procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: National-stage and published international application status requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is a national stage application or claims benefit of a published international application, requesters are entitled to status information if they supply a copy of the first page of the published international application or corresponding PCT Gazette page; status request should be made in writing to the Office of PCT Legal Administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only limited data (serial number, filing date, and whether pending/abandoned/patented) may be given for national stage applications and for applications claiming benefit of the published international application. Other continuity data remains confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit and explicit foreign filing license mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Permission to file abroad may be obtained either by (1) an implicit petition for a foreign filing license (every U.S. origin application filed in the USPTO is considered to include an implicit petition), or (2) an explicit petition under 37 CFR 5.12(b); alternatively, an applicant may wait 6 months after filing in the USPTO at which time a license is no longer required unless a Secrecy Order has been imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application is not marked by security screeners, the implicit petition is considered granted and the filing receipt will show 'Foreign Filing License Granted' and a date. Explicit petitions (37 CFR 5.12(b)) are useful where the filing receipt license is not granted, the filing receipt has not been issued, there is no corresponding U.S. application, additional subject matter is sought to be licensed, or expedited handling is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope, conversion, and fees for foreign filing licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Licenses granted from petitions have scope indicated on the license (broad scope per 37 CFR 5.15(a) or narrower per 5.15(b)); applicants granted narrow-scope licenses may petition under 37 CFR 5.15(c) to convert to broad scope for a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions under 5.14(a)/(b) and any license granted are given paper numbers and endorsed on the file wrapper; conversion petitions charge a fee per 37 CFR 1.17(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactive foreign filing licenses (37 CFR 5.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: A retroactive license may be sought if an unlicensed foreign filing occurred through error and without deceptive intent, but requirements of 37 CFR 5.25 must be fulfilled (countries, dates, nature of error, and oath/declaration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retroactive licenses are made retroactive only with respect to specific acts of foreign filing; detailed evidence and sworn statements are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of foreign filing licenses and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon written notification from the USPTO, any foreign filing license granted by 37 CFR 5.11(a) may be revoked; revocation ordinarily indicates referral to defense agencies. Revocation becomes effective on the date notice is mailed and does not necessarily preclude granting a narrower license under 5.12(b). Filings prior to revocation need not be abandoned, but additional filings without a license are not permitted unless 6 months have elapsed from filing of any corresponding U.S. application. Only imposition of a Secrecy Order will cause revocation of the authority under 35 U.S.C. 184 to file a foreign patent application 6 months after U.S. filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If revocation occurs, applicants may need to seek explicit petitions or otherwise comply with export/control restrictions; Papers needed for prosecution of foreign filings may be sent abroad only if they comply with export regulations. When a Secrecy Order is issued, restrictions must be immediately observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for failing to obtain necessary foreign filing license
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties under 35 U.S.C. 182, 185, and 186 include loss of patenting rights in addition to possible fine or imprisonment for failing to obtain any necessary license to file a patent application abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should seek licenses or wait the statutory 6-month period unless confident in an implicit license; retroactive relief is limited and requires satisfying 37 CFR 5.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements to DOE and NASA (property rights/statutory statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: No patent may be issued for an invention useful in production/utilization of special nuclear material or atomic energy (42 U.S.C. 2182) or with significant utility in aeronautical/space activities (42 U.S.C. 2457) unless the applicant files, with the application or within 30 days after request, a statement under oath setting forth the full facts surrounding conception/making and relationships to contracts with the Commission/Administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensing and Review will mail informal '45-Day Letters' to applicants whose applications are marked as of interest to DOE/NASA; responses within 45 days expedite processing. If no response or defective response, a formal statutory 30-day request is made; failure to timely file a proper statement will result in application being held abandoned (revivable under 37 CFR 1.137).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and form of DOE/NASA statements ('full facts')
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutes require statements to set forth 'the full facts' surrounding conception and making of the invention, including unique facts; use of broad form paragraphs alone is not ordinarily adequate. The statement must be in oath/declaration form and signed by the inventor(s) (applicant construed to mean inventor(s)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant lacks first-hand knowledge on contractual matters, the statement should identify the source of information or be accompanied by a supplemental declaration from an assignee or other person with requisite knowledge. If an inventor is deceased or unavailable, sworn statements from an assignee officer/employee with sufficient knowledge may be accepted after diligent efforts to obtain inventor's statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign DOE/NASA statements and supplemental requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements should be signed by the inventor(s); if inventorship is corrected during pendency, supplemental statements by added inventor(s) are required. If inventor is deceased/incompetent/unavailable or refuses after diligent efforts, substitute sworn statements by an assignee officer/employee with knowledge may be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute statements should be based on actual unavailability rather than convenience. Statements must include truthful assertions; willful false statements are punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001 and may jeopardize patent validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable sample statement format and required warnings
rubrics_metrics.description: An acceptable declaration format includes inventor identity, application number/title/date, employment relationship (if any), whether invention was made within scope of employment/with employer's facilities/funds, other relevant facts, and explicit statements addressing DOE/NASA contract relationships. The declaration must include a warning about penalties for false statements (18 U.S.C. 1001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms are illustrative; statements must accurately reflect the fact situation at the time made. Use of standardized, overly general forms is discouraged; include specific unique facts. Signatures, addresses, and dates must be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and handling of DOE/NASA property-rights papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Property rights statements to DOE or NASA may be filed at any time but should be updated if necessary before allowance; papers pertaining to property rights not associated with the application file must be sent immediately to the Licensing and Review section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely response to informal letters expedites processing. Licensing and Review maintains oversight and will send formal statutory requests if informal correspondence is not satisfactorily answered.
